=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/validate_driver.sh:102 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The bracket expression `[-A-Za-z0-9_./~%?\&=+:]` contains `\&` which in POSIX ERE matches literal backslash in addition to ampersand. The Python renderer regex at `scripts/render_validation_templates.py:352` uses `[A-Za-z0-9_./~%?&=+:-]` with just `&` and no backslash. The two URL validators intended to enforce the same rules disagree on whether backslash is allowed in path components.
  WHY: A direct environment-supplied APP_URL containing a literal backslash in the path would pass the shell driver validation but would have been rejected by the renderer-level validation if supplied via manifest. The renderer gate runs first for manifest-supplied values so no exploitable path exists in practice, but the inconsistency between the two validators could cause future maintenance errors when one regex is updated and the other is not.
- scripts/render_validation_templates.py:352 | RISK_SCORE=1
  PROBLEM: The regex character class `[A-Za-z0-9_./~%?&=+:-]` uses `+:-` which Python interprets as a character range from `+` (0x2B) to `:` (0x3A) rather than three individual characters. The range inadvertently admits comma (0x2C) in addition to the intended `+`, `-`, and `:` characters.
  WHY: The regex does not match its stated intent and could surprise a future maintainer.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/validate_driver.sh:102 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The shell regex character class [ -A-Za-z0-9_./~%?&=+:] includes a literal backslash `\` because of the POSIX ERE behavior where `\&` matches a literal `\`.
  WHY: This regex is less restrictive than the Python counterpart at scripts/render_validation_templates.py:352. While the current renderer gate prevents manifest-supplied backslashes from passing, this inconsistency risks security bypasses if the renderer logic is updated or bypassed in the future, as it enforces different validation rules on the same URL destination.
- scripts/render_validation_templates.py:340-348 | RISK_SCORE=2
  PROBLEM: The exclusion list for env_overrides misses sensitive curl and SSL configuration variables that could be used to exfiltrate data or compromise TLS (e.g., SSL_CLIENT_CERT, SSL_CLIENT_KEY, SSL_CLIENT_PASSWORD).
  WHY: The reviewer suggests adding "SSL_" to the startswith tuple in scripts/render_validation_templates.py to reject all SSL-related environment variable overrides at the renderer level.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/render_validation_templates.py:352 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The path character class `[A-Za-z0-9_./~%?&=+:-]` contains `+:-` which Python parses as a range from `+` (0x2B) to `:` (0x3A). That range uniquely admits `,` (0x2C) — a character the corresponding bash regex `[-A-Za-z0-9_./~%?\&=+:]` at scripts/validate_driver.sh:102 rejects.
  WHY: The two validators are intended to enforce the same rule but disagree: e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:8080/foo,bar` passes the renderer but is rejected by the driver. No test exercises a `,` in the URL path (test_render_validation_templates.py:175-178 and test_validate_driver_synthesised_filter.py:210-217 only list non-`,` reject cases), so the divergence is uncovered.
- scripts/render_validation_templates.py:352 | RISK_SCORE=2
  PROBLEM: The `+:-` tail is parsed as the 0x2B-0x3A range, admitting `,` (0x2C) — only Python sees it; the bash counterpart at scripts/validate_driver.sh:102 does not.
  WHY: The reviewer suggests fixing the Python path character class and optionally extending the existing test to include `http://127.0.0.1:8080/foo,bar` in the reject set.
- scripts/validate_driver.sh:690 | RISK_SCORE=2
  PROBLEM: The renderer `CURL_` startswith at scripts/render_validation_templates.py:347 blocks manifest-supplied values, but the host runner may already export `CURL_CA_PATH` / `CURL_CAPATH` / `CURL_CERTINFO`, all of which libcurl honours and which would still reach curl at probe time.
  WHY: The reviewer suggests extending the existing `env -u` chain with `-u CURL_CA_PATH -u CURL_CAPATH -u CURL_CERTINFO`.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- scripts/validate_driver.sh:102 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The shell regex bracket expression `[-A-Za-z0-9_./~%?\&=+:]` contains `\&` which in POSIX ERE (bash's `[[ =~ ]]` operator) treats backslash as literal within bracket expressions, so the character class admits both `\` and `&`. The Python renderer regex at scripts/render_validation_templates.py:352 uses `[A-Za-z0-9_./~%?&=+:-]` which admits only `&` (no backslash).
  WHY: A URL containing a literal backslash in the path component would pass the driver-side shell validation but would have been rejected by the renderer-side Python validation. The two validators intended to enforce the same URL format differ in their allowed character set. However, since the renderer gate runs first for manifest-supplied values (the manifest is rejected before validate.env is written), and curl does not interpret backslash specially in URLs, this inconsistency has no exploitable path in practice. The divergence could cause future maintenance confusion if a developer updates one regex but not the other believing they are identical.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- scripts/validate_driver.sh:690 | RISK_SCORE=1
  PROBLEM: The env -u list unsets known curl config/proxy vars but does not unset NETRC, which curl honors for credential auto-discovery from a .netrc file.
  WHY: The reviewer says this is not exploitable because the probe target is locked to 127.0.0.1 and the response is discarded, but adding -u NETRC would close the last curl configuration surface.
- scripts/render_validation_templates.py:341 | RISK_SCORE=1
  PROBLEM: The prefix list catches CURL_ but not the bare NETRC env var name. A manifest could set env_overrides.NETRC to point at a file path.
  WHY: The reviewer says this is not exploitable in context because the driver restricts to 127.0.0.1, but for consistency with the driver-side env -u hardening, the renderer should also reject it.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
